title: Formal Verification of Input Validation: A High-Coverage Security Property for Near-Term Deployment

original_idea.body:
# Formal Verification of Input Validation: A High-Coverage Security Property for Near-Term Deployment

**Problem:** Input validation (rejecting inputs outside expected ranges, formats, or sizes) is a simple but critical security property. Whether LLM-generated Lean 4 proofs can achieve high coverage for input validation properties — a tractable near-term deployment target — is unknown.

**Direction:** Collect 30 real input validation functions (email validators, URL parsers, integer range checkers) from open-source projects. Ask LLMs to generate Lean 4 formal specs and proofs for each. Measure success rate. Compare to fuzz testing as an alternative validation method.

**Why it matters:** Input validation failures cause 30%+ of web vulnerabilities (OWASP). If LLM-assisted formal verification of input validation achieves 80%+ success rate, it represents a deployable near-term safety improvement for AI-generated web code.

**Relevant context:** RAND (2026) lists automating input validation as a key benchmark target. No study measures LLM-assisted formal verification specifically for input validation. This is a tractable, high-impact, near-term application.
